There’s another city inside London, with its own government, its own police and its own mayor.

This tiny spot on the map is the City of London, also known as the Square Mile. It’s only about three square kilometers, but it’s two thousand years old. The Romans founded it under the name Londinium.

The body that runs the city is called the “City of London Corporation.” It’s considered one of the oldest local governments in the world that is still working. It even has its own observer in Parliament.

The city’s mayor is called the Lord Mayor. And this person is a completely different person from the Mayor of London, who runs all of Greater London. Greater London is made up of thirty-two boroughs, and this small area is counted separately from them.

At official ceremonies, even the king is specially welcomed at the city’s old border. The Lord Mayor presents him with the Pearl Sword. This centuries-old ceremony symbolically recognizes the city’s historic rights.

posts.text:
Here is the Root Cause Analysis (RCA) perspective on the FAA outage:

Adding 22 new systems or patches into the production environment created a data storm that overloaded the legacy FTI routers. 

Whether the underlying facility layer is bonded T1, DS3, or OC3, TDM is a synchronous switching technology from the 1990s built on 64kb channels. Because it's synchronous, it enforces hard physical limits on capacity and overhead. Those legacy routers only have shallow buckets of cache—so when the cache fills, packets become fully discard-eligible. Data is resent, escalating the issue. 

The result is a self-inflicted data storm, effectively acting as a Denial of Service (DoS) on their own network.

This is a mistake made by overconfident architects with limited experience and wisdom. They likely benched the software on a modern lab network without understanding the physical constraints of the production environment. 

An AI model won't catch a transport-layer bottleneck unless an engineer explicitly feeds it the legacy network topology, and assuming AI knows more than it does only blinds them to the basics of systems engineering.

Since this is a federal system, it likely relies on multiple ingress/egress points and/or rings from distinct entry vectors with hard switchovers. 

The short fix is adding modern load balancers at the edge to absorb bursts, paired with federal Starlink (Starshield) and DVB-S riding on existing federal satellites for out-of-band burst capacity. 

The physical location of airports has always been a limiting factor for getting broadband to the curb, and legacy regulations are built to be broken.

Even better, using multicast over satcom would make the overall mesh far more efficient than the "as-built" terrestrial setup. Pushing updates and common data once instead of 22 separate times. 

The only catch is that moving from stateful unicast to stateless satellite multicast would likely require an entire software rewrite. Trenching fiber takes time for the permanent fix.

🚨 DISTURBING RUMOR FROM THE DARK WEB

Before anything else, let me be absolutely clear: This is NOT a confirmed report. There is no sufficient credible evidence to support these claims, and I am NOT presenting any of this as fact.

However, after everything that happened yesterday, it’s hard not to feel concerned when scenarios like this start circulating.

I received information from an unverified source, allegedly originating from the dark web, describing a potential global cyber event supposedly scheduled for November 17.

Here’s what the message claims:

↓ BEGIN UNVERIFIED QUOTE ↓

“Everything connected to the internet will be hacked.

A so-called ‘COVID 2.0’ will begin. Major banks will be compromised, and financial records will be completely erased.

Thousands of bank accounts will suddenly display a balance of $0, with no way to recover or verify their original balances.

This will trigger a global internet lockdown.

The entire world’s internet infrastructure will allegedly be shut down for three months.

During that period, an extremely advanced artificial intelligence system will supposedly be used to identify and fix vulnerabilities and security flaws across the network.

The consequences will be widespread panic, confusion, and unprecedented global disruption.

People are being urged to stockpile food, water, gold, silver, weapons, ammunition, and cash as quickly as possible.

The alleged worldwide shutdown will begin on November 17.”

↑ END UNVERIFIED QUOTE ↑

⚠️ My perspective:

I want to emphasize once again that there is no reliable evidence confirming this scenario or the November 17 date. It could be nothing more than an elaborate conspiracy theory or deliberate fearmongering.

But considering the cybersecurity incidents and disruptions we’ve witnessed recently, it’s understandable why these kinds of rumors might make people uneasy.

I’m sharing this for discussion, not as a warning that these events will actually happen.

The question is not whether we should believe this rumor.

The question is: How vulnerable is our global digital infrastructure to a truly coordinated cyberattack?

What do you think? Is this just another internet conspiracy, or a reminder of how dependent we’ve become on systems we barely understand?

🚨BREAKING (EXCLUSIVE): National Security Concerns Leaked by MSFT Whistleblower

Leaked Microsoft screenshots show an India-based engineer received approval to view U.S. government cloud logs.

A Microsoft whistleblower contacted me and shared screenshots supporting allegations that Microsoft used its “escort” process to allow an India based engineer to access Government Community Cloud (GCC) systems. The whistleblower alleges the engineer is not a U.S. citizen. 

Microsoft’s own published rules state that temporary elevated access to customer content in GCC requires verified U.S. citizenship. The escort model is the workaround the company uses so non-U.S. personnel can still direct the work.

The screenshots show Viraj Chokhany requesting and receiving approval for escort access to view logs in the DPRODMGD151 environment, which is part of Government Community Cloud Moderate — the cloud used by many federal, state, and local agencies.

In the escort process, a U.S. person is supposed to open the system while the India-based engineer guides the work. 

The whistleblower believes this raises urgent national security concerns and may violate FedRAMP requirements.

Multiple Microsoft employees have reviewed the screenshots and confirmed they appear authentic. Viraj, has been confirmed to live in India-- Where he also attended and graduated college. 

The whistleblower is working on a public statement. I will release the whistleblowers statement when I receive it. 

Attached images are some of the screenshots that I received from the Whistleblower. 

@DHSgov @FBIDirectorKash @JDVance

China's automotive industry is facing a historic slowdown:

China’s automotive industry profit margin fell to 3.6% in the first 8 months of 2026, its lowest in at least 12 years.

This is now on track for its 12th consecutive annual decline.

Years of heavy investment have created severe production overcapacity, while weakening domestic demand is intensifying price wars among car manufacturers.

Meanwhile, in the first 8 months of 2026, domestic passenger vehicle sales dropped -22% YoY.

For the full year, car sales are expected to fall -22% YoY, to 18.5 million, their lowest annual total since 2014.

Now, factories have the capacity to produce a record ~62.9 million vehicles this year, more than 3 times the expected sales figure.

China’s auto industry is struggling.

Private economists estimate the economy contracted for two consecutive quarters in 2026, with one forecast putting the third-quarter decline at 2.66%.

Growth forecasts for the year have been slashed to around 1% or less, far below the government's 3% target. Even the IMF has cut its projection from 3.5% to 2.1%.

Consumer spending remains weak, private-sector employment fell by roughly 13,000 jobs in July, and borrowing has struggled to recover.

Meanwhile, Argentina's country-risk premium has climbed above 700 basis points, adding to concerns about the country's financial outlook.

Milei's economic reforms now face a major test as the promised recovery struggles to gain momentum.
